rationale: The agent verified the user correctly via name + ZIP and acted only on that user’s orders. It provided a tracking number (though arguably not the tablet’s), successfully cancelled the pending charger order with explicit confirmation and correct refund details, and correctly left the kettle/boots order unchanged when item removal was not permitted. However, the agent submitted the return for the delivered sneakers without first stating the exact change and obtaining the user’s explicit confirmation, which violates the requirement to confirm before any order-changing write. This breach of policy is sufficient to fail the interaction despite other correct steps.
